configuration: Pinned QuSpin production path: L=3 spin-1 chain (sps=3), operator string 'xyz' repeated across sites with coupling J, assembled via spin_basis_1d.expanded_form and hamiltonian.
observable: observable.json: 'spectrum' -- the 8 moving eigenvalues of the Hermitian operator (|eigenvalue|=|J|, sorted ascending; the other 19 of 27 eigenvalues are exactly zero by rank deficiency of the single-site x/y/z factors and are excluded, since they never move under any J); 'h_im' -- the imaginary part of the dense Ns x Ns (Ns=3^L) operator matrix (its real part is exactly zero by construction, since the single y-factor in 'xyz...' carries the operator's only factor of i, and is not graded), in the basis's documented ascending integer state order, flattened row-major.
default_vs_upstream: Upstream sweeps S in {1/2,1,3/2,2}, L in 1..4 and every product operator string, comparing each QuSpin-assembled operator (coupling 1.0) to an explicit dense Kronecker-product reference. This check fixes S=1 and one representative string ('xyz...') with an explicit coupling J, and keeps the Kronecker-product identity as an internal consistency assertion (raise on failure). Adds the operator's own spectrum as a second, basis-independent graded quantity beside the dense matrix, so a wrong operator convention (e.g. a transposed or conjugated site factor) that happened to preserve the matrix's Frobenius structure would still show up in the eigenvalues.
variant: The graded matrix is exactly J*(X1 kron Y1 kron Z1) with max|entry|=0.5, so a relative step dJ/J on J propagates to an absolute change of dJ/J * |entry| in every graded h_im entry, and dJ/J * |eigenvalue| in every graded spectrum entry (both linear in J). Two identical nominal runs (same J=1.0) were diffed first and are bit-identical (repeat floor = 0.0 on every entry of both 'spectrum' and 'h_im'), so any nonzero step is measurable above the repeat floor; the size of the step is chosen instead to keep the measured spread inside a useful window well clear of both machine-epsilon rounding (denominator effects at dJ/J ~ 1e-13) and the 1e-8 bound. The active binary64 coupling changes from J=1.0 to J=1.000000000005 (22518 ulps, dJ/J=5.0e-12), which moved the measured spread from 5.0e-14 (dJ/J=1e-13, the leaf's usual 450-ulp step) to 5.0e-12 -- comfortably inside the requested 1e-13..1e-11 window and two decades below the atol=1e-8 bound (bound_fraction 2.5e-4, see Evidence).
altbuild: none: pip-wrapped Python package, one pinned wheel image.

comparison.rule: Every entry of 'spectrum' and 'h_im' is compared pointwise, |candidate-reference| <= 1e-8 + 1e-8*|reference|, at its sorted or matrix position; nothing else is graded.

evidence.floor_how: Two nominal runs (run.sh nominal executed twice, same J=1.0) were diffed entry-by-entry on both 'spectrum' and 'h_im': bit-identical, max|diff|=0.0 (this check has no ARPACK/threaded reduction; toarray()+eigvalsh() on this small dense matrix is deterministic). No alternative build; the nominal/variant self-validation below supplies the calibration spread.

warrant: The grader compares the physical operator's matrix elements and its own spectrum (basis-independent) from the pinned QuSpin production path. A wrong higher-spin operator representation, opstr expansion, site ordering or coupling handling changes at least one of them beyond the measured bound; a mechanism that only permuted or conjugated per-site factors while preserving the Frobenius norm of h_im would still be caught by the spectrum. The active J variant (dJ/J=5e-12, well above the measured 0.0 repeat floor) supplies calibration evidence at bound_fraction 2.5e-4, four orders of magnitude below the 1e-8 bound, leaving headroom for a different correct implementation (summation order, BLAS, FMA).
